svg.title: Mod-native JavaScript with owned HTML and optional rendering providers
svg.desc: JavaScript Runtime 0.1.0 adapts Jint 2.11.10 to the ES5.1 prototype profile as Workshop mod source. A C# consumer explicitly supplies code, owns its local HTML endpoint and grants node and data IDs. The interpreter exposes no arbitrary CLR or game objects. One private claim binds a realm to an actual document. Events and timers submit one validated atomic mutation candidate; its committed frame supplies input coordinates. HTML Frontend 0.2.1 and HDR API 0.9.11 map retained artwork and provider slots onto HUD, plane, cylinder, sphere, ellipsoid or UV mesh. Registered mod-native providers require no renderer plugin; native camera, texture and pointer features use separately checked optional Client Renderer 0.9.14 capabilities. Missing native capability returns Requires plugin before attachment. Script errors retire callbacks while preserving the accepted display. Explicit cleanup removes only runtime-owned HUDs. CSS animations and broader browser features remain planned; the parser still rejects script markup.
svg.text: JavaScript stays in the mod; rendering stays modular
ALPHA · JS 0.1.0 · HTML 0.2.1 · core 0.9.11 / scene 20 · client-local

g.text: No external runtime or game bridge
One detached candidate · validate → layout → publish → commit
Coalesced text / data / source choices · exact provider source-check before attachment
Failed callback drops staged writes; failed publication restores or retires visible output explicitly
Claim release during publication cancels commit · native LCD JS admission rejects without a sequential fallback
HTML Frontend 0.2.1 → HDR retained canvas and shared surface mapper
Vector / SVG / text + independently owned provider slots
HUD · plane · cylinder · sphere · ellipsoid · authored UV mesh
Cooperative input uses the accepted frame and the same inverse surface mapping
Owned lifecycle · safe optional extensions · broader features planned
Script failure preserves the accepted display; explicit cleanup removes only runtime-owned HUDs
No script tags, browser DOM/network, Date, regex or eval · CSS timelines, Canvas and GPU effects are separate work
